suggestions: reorder joins to reduce intermediate rows
optimized_sql:
WITH store_base AS (
    SELECT sr.sr_customer_sk AS customer_sk,
           sr.sr_item_sk AS item_sk,
           ss.ss_store_sk AS store_sk,
           MAX(ss.ss_net_profit) AS store_sales_profit,
           MAX(sr.sr_net_loss) AS store_returns_loss
    FROM store_sales ss
    INNER JOIN store_returns sr
      ON ss.ss_customer_sk = sr.sr_customer_sk
     AND ss.ss_item_sk = sr.sr_item_sk
     AND ss.ss_ticket_number = sr.sr_ticket_number
    INNER JOIN date_dim d1
      ON ss.ss_sold_date_sk = d1.d_date_sk
    INNER JOIN date_dim d2
      ON sr.sr_returned_date_sk = d2.d_date_sk
    WHERE d1.d_moy = 4
      AND d1.d_year = 1999
      AND d2.d_moy BETWEEN 4 AND 10
      AND d2.d_year = 1999
    GROUP BY sr.sr_customer_sk, sr.sr_item_sk, ss.ss_store_sk
),
catalog_profits AS (
    SELECT sb.customer_sk AS customer_sk,
           sb.item_sk AS item_sk,
           MAX(cs.cs_net_profit) AS catalog_profit
    FROM store_base sb
    INNER JOIN catalog_sales cs
      ON cs.cs_bill_customer_sk = sb.customer_sk
     AND cs.cs_item_sk = sb.item_sk
    INNER JOIN date_dim d3
      ON cs.cs_sold_date_sk = d3.d_date_sk
    WHERE d3.d_moy BETWEEN 4 AND 10
      AND d3.d_year = 1999
    GROUP BY sb.customer_sk, sb.item_sk
)
SELECT i.i_item_id AS i_item_id,
       i.i_item_desc AS i_item_desc,
       st.s_store_id AS s_store_id,
       st.s_store_name AS s_store_name,
       MAX(b.store_sales_profit) AS store_sales_profit,
       MAX(b.store_returns_loss) AS store_returns_loss,
       MAX(cp.catalog_profit) AS catalog_sales_profit
FROM store_base b
INNER JOIN catalog_profits cp
  ON cp.customer_sk = b.customer_sk
 AND cp.item_sk = b.item_sk
INNER JOIN item i
  ON i.i_item_sk = b.item_sk
INNER JOIN store st
  ON st.s_store_sk = b.store_sk
GROUP BY i.i_item_id, i.i_item_desc, st.s_store_id, st.s_store_name
ORDER BY i.i_item_id, i.i_item_desc, st.s_store_id, st.s_store_name
LIMIT 100
